module_title: NITI, NHRC & CBI - Composition and Appointment
introduction: This level focuses on 'how' these bodies are structured and 'who' appoints their members. This is the most crucial part for state PSCs and SSC exams.

core_concepts.title: Cooperative Federalism (NITI Aayog)
core_concepts.description: NITI Aayog follows a 'Bottom-Up' approach where states are equal partners. This is managed through the Governing Council (CMs of all states and LGs of UTs).

core_concepts.title: NHRC Appointment Committee
core_concepts.description: The President appoints the NHRC members based on the recommendation of a 6-member committee: PM, Speaker of LS, Deputy Chairman of RS, Leaders of Opposition in both houses, and Union Home Minister.

core_concepts.title: CBI Appointment Committee
core_concepts.description: The Director of CBI is appointed by a 3-member committee: Prime Minister, Leader of Opposition/Single Largest Party in LS, and Chief Justice of India (or a nominee SC Judge).

core_concepts.title: Powers of NHRC
core_concepts.description: NHRC has the powers of a Civil Court. It can summon witnesses and request public records, but its recommendations are NOT binding on the government.

important_entities.name: Governing Council
important_entities.significance: Includes all CMs; replaces the NDC (National Development Council) in practice.

important_entities.name: CEO of NITI Aayog
important_entities.significance: A professional head with a fixed tenure, usually a senior bureaucrat.

important_entities.name: Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT)
important_entities.significance: Though originally under Home Ministry, CBI now falls under DoPT (Ministry of Personnel).

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: The Chairman of Rajya Sabha (Vice President) is NOT part of the NHRC appointment committee. It is the **Deputy Chairman** who is a member.
NHRC is a recommendatory body. It cannot punish the guilty or award relief on its own; it can only recommend the government to do so.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: PM, Home Minister + 2 Presiding Officers (Speaker/Deputy Chair) + 2 Leaders of Opposition.
CBI is currently under the Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances, and Pensions.

exam_strategy_tips: Focus on the 'Leader of Opposition' as a member of appointment committees—this is a high-yield fact.
Remember that the CEO of NITI Aayog is appointed by the PM, not the President.
